author: @RAVIELLORE
text:
The Colombo Whisper: Is Washington Forcing India’s Hand?

​The shadows of Colombo and Bangkok are getting crowded. Behind closed doors, retired generals, ex-spies, and seasoned diplomats from India and Pakistan are clinking teacups and talking crisis management. But let’s cut through the diplomatic fluff: Track-II diplomacy is rarely just a casual chat among old rivals.

​With these backchannel whispers growing louder since mid-2025, a glaring question hangs over the subcontinent: Is this a genuine attempt at regional sanity, or is Washington quietly twisting arms to force a shotgun wedding?

​The Desperation and the Playbook
​Let’s look at the board. Ever since the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty—a move that fundamentally altered the geopolitical calculus—Islamabad has been on a relentless international PR blitz. Facing economic headwinds and a shifting global landscape, Pakistan has turned up the volume, knocking on every door from global think tanks to Western media outlets, begging for an intervention.

​And Washington? They’re listening.

​Following the fallout of Operation Sindoor, the U.S. has been practically tripping over itself to issue blandly polite statements "welcoming dialogue" at neutral venues. But underneath the diplomatic niceties lies a cold, hard reality:

​The American Dilemma: Washington is terrified of a two-front nuclear flashpoint distracting from its broader Indo-Pacific strategy. If the U.S. doesn't engage, it risks alienating a critical partner in New Delhi or letting a volatile region spin entirely out of control.

​New Delhi’s Line in the Sand
​Despite the heavy hitters reportedly sitting at the table—including unconfirmed whispers of former Indian Army Chief General Manoj Naravane lending his weight to the Colombo talks—India’s official stance hasn't budged an inch.

​New Delhi’s position remains fiercely uncompromising: You cannot trade bullets and olive branches at the same time.

​The Core Mandate: No official Track-I talks without verifiable, concrete destruction of terror infrastructure across the border.

​The Reality Check: While retired officials can map out "what-if" scenarios all day, they don't hold the keys to South Block.

​The Bottom Line
​International arm-twisting can buy you a seat at a secret table in Sri Lanka, but it cannot buy peace. Washington can pressure, cajole, and nudge all it wants, but Uncle Sam doesn’t live in this neighborhood.
​Until Islamabad delivers more than just diplomatic theater and addresses India's hardline security anxieties, these Track-II summits are just expensive coffee mornings. The steering wheel of South Asian stability remains firmly in the hands of the locals—and New Delhi isn't about to let an external power dictate its map.

🚨 | The S-400 Is NOT India’s Shield.

It’s Just One Layer.

“The most dangerous misconception in modern warfare is believing that one weapon wins wars.”

Following Operation Sindoor, social media conversations have increasingly portrayed the Russian S-400 as India’s “ultimate air defence system.”

That narrative misses the bigger picture.

📍 OSINT tells a very different story.

India is quietly building something far more significant:

A layered national air defence network.

🧠 Think Beyond The S-400

The S-400 is designed to engage long-range threats—fighter aircraft, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles—at distances of up to 400 km.

But no modern military relies on a single interceptor.

Instead, India is integrating multiple defensive layers.

These include:

• S-400 Triumf (Long-range interception)
• MR-SAM / Barak-8 (Medium-range area defence)
• Akash & Akash-NG (Point and tactical air defence)
• SPYDER systems (Short-range quick reaction)
• Indigenous Project Kusha (Future long-range shield)
• Integrated Air Command & Control System (IACCS) linking sensors and shooters across services.

The objective isn’t to build the world’s best missile.

It’s to build the world’s hardest airspace to penetrate.

⚠️ Why This Matters

Recent conflicts have demonstrated a simple reality:

No interceptor has a 100% kill probability.

Layering compensates for that.

If one system misses…

Another engages.

If radar is jammed…

Passive sensors continue tracking.

If one battery relocates…

Another already covers the gap.

That’s how survivability is engineered.

🎯 The Strategic Shift

Recent reports indicate India has begun receiving its fourth S-400 regiment, while long-term plans continue to strengthen indigenous air-defence programmes. The real story isn’t merely another missile battery.

It’s the emergence of an integrated air-defence architecture where imported and indigenous systems operate together.

🔍 Information Warfare Watch

Pakistan’s information ecosystem frequently frames the S-400 as the single centre of gravity for India’s air defence.

That framing is strategically convenient.

Because it ignores the larger reality:

Neutralising one battery is not equivalent to neutralising an integrated air-defence network.

The strength of India’s air defence lies less in any individual platform than in the way multiple systems are networked into a layered architecture.

In modern warfare, integration is often a greater force multiplier than any single weapon.

text:
THE UKRAINE LESSON PAKISTAN IS STUDYING - AND THE STRATEGIC GAP INDIA CANNOT AFFORD TO IGNORE

An Analysis of the New Warfare Doctrine and What It Means for the India-Pakistan Equation

Start With Russia. End With India.

Right now, as you read this, approximately 330 drones and missiles are simultaneously flying toward Russian territory. Tonight alone.

Since late 2022, Russia has routinely employed almost one thousand drones per night in attack waves against Ukrainian targets, exploiting their relatively low cost to exhaust air defenses. Russia - one of the two nuclear superpowers of the Cold War era, possessor of the world's largest nuclear arsenal, with a defence industrial complex that once armed half the planet - is being systematically bled by a country that on June 22, 2022 sent its very first strike drone toward Russian territory. A single civilian commercial drone bought from China.

By 2025, Ukraine was producing 10 million drones annually. By 2026, projections exceed 25 million units across various classes. 80–85% of frontline targets are now engaged by UAVs.

What Ukraine did to Russia in three years is the most important military transformation of the 21st century. And Pakistan's military establishment - staffed with some of the most serious students of modern warfare in South Asia, has been watching every frame of it.

India must understand what they have been learning.

📌 CHAPTER I: THE UKRAINE DOCTRINE - HOW A WEAK STATE DEFEATED CONVENTIONAL MILITARY LOGIC

In 2014, Ukrainian soldiers were throwing their phones into the air hoping a text message to their commanders would connect. Their military was hollowed out, under-equipped, and structurally dependent on Soviet-era doctrine and equipment.

Since February 2022, the conflict in Ukraine has served as a vast laboratory for the use of drones on a high-intensity battlefield. Within months, these systems became indispensable, reshaping doctrines, saturating defenses, and driving a permanent technological war of attrition.

The transformation was not gradual. It was revolutionary. And it followed a precise sequence:

Phase 1 - 2022: Mass deployment. Ukraine launched its Army of Drones programme through crowdfunding, distributing UAVs down to company level and training thousands of operators. The drone became a tactical survival tool, used for reconnaissance and artillery fire adjustment.

Phase 2 - 2022–2023: Rise of strikes and counterstrikes. Both sides strengthened air and electromagnetic defences. MALE drones virtually disappeared from the tactical battlefield. Kamikaze systems and loitering munitions - Iranian Shaheds deployed in swarms - began to dominate. A drone's battlefield lifespan was measured in individual flights.

Phase 3 - 2024–2025: AI integration. FPV drones evolved with fiber-optic tethers impervious to jamming, extending range to 20 kilometres. Long-range models reach hundreds of kilometres, targeting logistics deep behind lines. Semi-autonomous killer drones identify targets via machine learning, processing video feeds in real time, reducing operator workload amid electronic warfare saturation.

The economic disruption this produced is staggering: NATO-sourced analysis confirms Ukrainian drones are responsible for more than 65% of destroyed Russian tanks. FPV drones priced under $500 each are destroying equipment worth millions.

This is the fundamental military-economic revolution of our era: the cost of destroying an asset has been permanently decoupled from the cost of building it. A $500 FPV drone destroys a $5 million tank. A $2,000 Shahed destroys a $50 million piece of infrastructure. The attacker's economics are catastrophically favourable. The defender's economics are catastrophically unfavourable.

Modern air defense must prioritize scale, cost control, and integration across many simple systems rather than dependence on a small number of high-end weapons. Initial reliance on expensive missiles against low-cost drones created an unsustainable model.

Russia has not "won" despite its overwhelming conventional superiority, nuclear arsenal, larger economy, and unlimited political will to fight. It has been bled into strategic exhaustion by a country that learned to substitute mass, low-cost, rapidly iterable drone production for every conventional military capability it lacked.

Pakistan's military planners have read every page of this.

📌 CHAPTER II: THE OPERATION SINDOOR CEASEFIRE - A STRATEGIC ASSESSMENT**

The argument that Operation Sindoor's ceasefire was a strategic blunder - comparable to Indira Gandhi's 1971 Shimla generosity or Lal Bahadur Shastri's 1965 Tashkent concession - deserves serious engagement, not dismissal.

The historical pattern is damning:

1965: India held Lahore's outskirts. Shastri accepted Tashkent under Soviet and American pressure. Pakistan returned to pre-war positions having learnt that initiating conflict with India carries no permanent territorial cost.

1971: India had Pakistan's 93,000 soldiers as prisoners and the option of dismantling Pakistan's western military capacity entirely. Indira Gandhi chose Shimla, returned the prisoners, and extracted no permanent strategic concession beyond the creation of Bangladesh. Pakistan rebuilt its military, developed nuclear weapons, and within two decades was running proxy terror operations in Punjab and Kashmir.

2025: India had destroyed Pakistan's air defence system, struck 13 air bases, demonstrated complete air superiority, and was 88 hours into an operation with momentum entirely in its favour. The ceasefire came at American pressure, channelled through Rubio's call to Asim Munir, before India's military objectives were complete.

The parallel argument: Pakistan now knows that India will strike hard but stop when American pressure arrives. That the nuclear bluff works - not because Pakistan would use nuclear weapons, but because the threat triggers American diplomatic intervention before India can achieve decisive results. That the cost of sponsoring terrorism against India is bounded and manageable.

Where the blunder argument has structural limits:

The 1965 and 1971 analogies are imperfect because both involved conventional military occupations of territory that create long-term liabilities. Operation Sindoor was a precision strike campaign - its objectives were destruction of terrorist infrastructure and establishment of deterrence doctrine, not territorial conquest. Both objectives were achieved. Continuing would have shifted from a successful limited operation to an open-ended war with escalation risks India's leadership calculated were not worth the additional gains.

The honest assessment: the blunder was not stopping - it was stopping without extracting a permanent structural concession. No demilitarisation of Pakistan's border zone. No international monitoring of terrorist camps. No American commitment to consequence if Pakistan restarts its terror infrastructure. The ceasefire was accepted without terms. That is where the 1965 and 1971 comparison bites.

📌 CHAPTER III: THE PAKISTAN RECALIBRATION - WHAT RAWALPINDI IS STUDYING RIGHT NOW

Pakistan's military establishment is not stupid. It is, in fact, one of the most institutionally sophisticated military organisations in the developing world - staffed by officers who study global conflicts with the intensity of people who know their next war is not hypothetical.

What lessons is GHQ Rawalpindi drawing from Ukraine?

Lesson 1 - Drone Swarm Saturation

Russia's strategy of pairing small-group infiltrations with bombardments using large numbers of tactical and long-range drones has paralysed ground forces and rendered airpower much less decisive. Regional exercises and war games in 2025 revealed a shocking lack of preparedness even in NATO.

Pakistan's application: A coordinated barrage of low-cost Turkish Bayraktar TB2s, Chinese Wing Loong IIs, and indigenously produced Shahpar drones - launched simultaneously from multiple vectors -toward Indian infrastructure targets. Not to achieve air superiority. To saturate and exhaust India's air defence expenditure. India's S-400, Akashteer, and Akash systems are sophisticated and expensive. Every interceptor costs multiples of what it destroys.

The drone revolution has created a new taxonomy: expendable assets, attritable assets, risk-tolerant assets, and survivable assets. Where commanders once faced a binary choice between risking high-value assets or foregoing operations entirely, they now have degrees of risk appropriate to different threat environments.

Pakistan can afford to lose 500 drones costing $2,000 each - $1 million total - if those drones force India to expend $500 million in air defence munitions. That is the Ukraine arithmetic applied to the India-Pakistan equation.

Lesson 2 - Infrastructure as the Strategic Target

Ukraine demonstrated that attacking energy infrastructure - power grids, dams, fuel depots, industrial nodes - degrades an adversary's war-making capacity without requiring territorial conquest or air superiority. The civilian suffering this produces also generates international pressure for ceasefire.

Pakistan's application: Adani ports, Gujarat petrochemical infrastructure, border power stations, and dam infrastructure in the western river systems. These targets require minimal drone accuracy - large structures hit by even partially functional drones cause significant damage. The satellite imagery of damage generates international pressure. The economic disruption compounds the military cost.

Lesson 3 - China and Turkey as the Resupply Chain

Ukraine's capacity to sustain drone warfare rests on its ability to produce 25 million drones annually, with international partners financing production in distributed European facilities.

Pakistan's equivalent: China can manufacture and deliver drone components to Pakistan faster than any Western arms control mechanism can respond. Turkish Bayraktars are politically insulated from American pressure - Turkey is a NATO member and will not accept US veto over its defence exports. In a drone attrition war, Pakistan's resupply chain is structurally more resilient than India's interception expenditure.

Lesson 4 - Chinese Satellite Support

Ukraine's battlefield advantage rests heavily on commercial satellite communications and intelligence - creating what is effectively an Internet of the Battlefield.

The Chinese equivalent is BeiDou and China's commercial imaging constellation. In a Pakistan-India conflict where China has explicit strategic interest in Pakistan's survival, Chinese satellite support for Pakistani targeting and communications is not a hypothetical. It is a planned capability.

📌 CHAPTER IV: INDIA'S STRUCTURAL VULNERABILITIES - THE HONEST ACCOUNTING

India's air defence performed brilliantly in May 2025. Akashteer achieved a 100% kill rate against Pakistani drone swarms. S-400 intercepted all incoming missiles. The success was real and should be acknowledged.

But Ukraine teaches that the question is not whether your air defence works in the first engagement. The question is whether it remains economically sustainable across months of attrition warfare.

Vulnerability 1 - The Interceptor Cost Asymmetry

Initial reliance on expensive missiles against low-cost drones created an unsustainable economic model. Air defence must prioritise scale, cost control, and integration across many simple systems.

India's Akash missile costs approximately ₹2.5 crore per unit. A Chinese FPV drone equivalent costs ₹15,000. The ratio is 1:166. If Pakistan can manufacture or source drones at scale - and China can ensure they can - the attrition economics favour Pakistan catastrophically in a long conflict.

Vulnerability 2 - No Deep Drone Manufacturing Ecosystem

After the outbreak of war in Ukraine, the number of drone manufacturing companies rose from 41 in 2022 to 183 in 2024. Ukraine now produces 4.5 million drones annually.

India has no equivalent drone manufacturing ecosystem at anything approaching this scale. Make in India defence initiatives are maturing but remain years from the kind of rapid-iteration, decentralised, startup-driven drone production that Ukraine developed under existential pressure.

Vulnerability 3 - Critical Infrastructure Concentration

India's major infrastructure - Adani ports, Gujarat petrochemical, Bhakra Nangal and other dam systems, western railway nodes - is geographically concentrated and not hardened against drone attack at the scale a saturation campaign would require. Ukraine's infrastructure survived three years of Russian strikes partly through dispersal, redundancy, and Western repair support. India has none of these buffers institutionalised.

📌 CHAPTER V: WHAT INDIA MUST BUILD - THE STRATEGIC IMPERATIVE**

The analysis above is not defeatist. It is diagnostic. India has significant structural advantages Pakistan does not: a larger economy growing at 7%+, a maturing defence industrial base, the S-400, a satellite constellation, and the demonstrated will to use force decisively.

But the Ukraine lesson demands specific institutional responses:

Response 1 - A Drone Manufacturing Industrial Policy

India needs the equivalent of Ukraine's Army of Drones programme - a nationally funded, startup-driven, rapid-iteration drone manufacturing ecosystem that can produce counter-drone interceptors at $500–2,000 per unit rather than $250,000 per Akash missile. iDEX has begun this work. It needs ten times the funding and a wartime urgency framing.

Response 2 - Infrastructure Hardening as Strategic Priority**

Critical national infrastructure - particularly in Gujarat and Rajasthan, the likely target zones in any Pakistan escalation - needs hardened protection, dispersed redundancy, and active drone defence perimeters. Ukraine's experience suggests that infrastructure protection requires a dedicated doctrine, not an afterthought to conventional military planning.

Response 3 - Demanding Structural Concessions Before Any Future Ceasefire

The lesson of 1965, 1971, and 2025 is identical: India wins the battle and accepts a ceasefire without structural concessions, leaving Pakistan free to recalibrate and return. The next ceasefire - if India initiates conflict again - must be conditional on verifiable, internationally monitored dismantlement of terror infrastructure. No terms, no ceasefire.

Response 4 - Countering the China-Turkey Resupply Chain Diplomatically

India must use its leverage with Turkey - a significant trade partner - and with Western capitals to establish in advance that Chinese or Turkish drone resupply to Pakistan during an active conflict constitutes a casus belli for economic consequences. The diplomatic groundwork must be laid before the shooting starts.

The Verdict

Ukraine is an early and highly accelerated case of a broader global shift in which drones are becoming a standard instrument of warfare. The operational, doctrinal, and ethical consequences of this shift will increasingly shape conflicts far beyond Europe.

Pakistan's military planners are not watching Ukraine as passive observers. They are running war games, updating doctrine, and building the drone acquisition pipeline that the Ukraine lesson demands. China and Turkey are willing suppliers. The attrition economics favour them in any extended conflict.

India won Operation Sindoor decisively. It established a new deterrence doctrine. It called Pakistan's nuclear bluff. These are genuine, historic achievements.

But the war that Pakistan is now planning - informed by three years of watching Ukraine bleed Russia through drone attrition, infrastructure targeting, and cost asymmetry warfare - will not look like May 2025. It will look like what Russia faces tonight: 330 drones in the air simultaneously, aimed at the things a country cannot afford to lose.

India needs to be building its answer to that war. Now. Not after the next Pahalgam.
summary: Analyzes Ukraine drone warfare lessons for India-Pakistan strategy.

text:
🇮🇳 India honours the bravehearts of Operation Sindoor

The names of six soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during Operation Sindoor have now been officially made public. Their names will also be engraved on a special commemorative brick at the National War Memorial, New Delhi, ensuring that their courage and sacrifice are remembered forever.

The six bravehearts are:

🕊️ Subedar Major Pawan Kumar
HQ, 10 Infantry Brigade

🕊️ Rifleman Sunil Kumar (Vir Chakra – Posthumous)
4th Battalion, Jammu & Kashmir Light Infantry

🕊️ Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar
5 Field Regiment

🕊️ Agniveer Mood Murali Naik
851 Light Regiment

🕊️ Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh
237 Field Workshop

🕊️ Sergeant Surinder Kumar (Vayu Medal – Posthumous)
39 Wing, Indian Air Force

President Droupadi Murmu recently conferred the Vir Chakra (Posthumous) on Rifleman Sunil Kumar in recognition of his exceptional gallantry.

Their sacrifice is a reminder of the courage, dedication and selfless service of India’s Armed Forces in defending the nation.

Salute to our fallen heroes. Their names will live forever in the heart of the Nation. 🇮🇳

People associated with the Congress and its ecosystem on social media are spreading the misconception that India has now, after a year, publicly disclosed information about the six military personnel who sacrificed their lives in Operation Sindoor.

The facts were already available in the public domain. The current debate is not about whether there were casualties or not, but about when the names of the martyrs were formally released and inscribed on the National War Memorial.

author: @abhijitmajumder
text:
FACT CHECK:
Bharat did not conceal the sacrifice of our brave soldiers. She honoured them.
India 🇮🇳 is not like Pakistan, which did not claim its soldiers’ bodies during Kargil war.
Those claiming India has only now revealed that six military personnel lost their lives during Operation Sindoor must revisit the press conference held on May 11, 2025, a day after the op was paused.
In that briefing, the then DGMO had clearly acknowledged the sacrifice of five soldiers and paid tribute to them.
The Chief of the Air Staff had also visited the family of the sole airman who was killed during Operation Sindoor.
Moreover, two of the fallen soldiers were honoured with gallantry awards. Rifleman Sunil Kumar received Vir Chakra (Posthumous), while Sergeant Surendra Kumar was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal (Gallantry) (Posthumous).
summary: Fact-checks India did not hide sacrifices, citing May 2025 DGMO tribute and gallantry awards.

author: @Datta_karan
text:
Most governments struggle to point to a dozen transformative changes across a decade. This list runs to a hundred and it spans everything from a missed call getting you a gas cylinder to India landing on the moon.

Start with the things that changed daily life so quietly most people forgot what came before.

UPI payment. DigiLocker. FASTag replacing toll queues. Online bill payment. Jan Dhan bank accounts bringing hundreds of millions of people into the formal financial system for the first time. Aadhaar linking that made welfare delivery direct and cut out the intermediaries who had been skimming it for generations. Free rations reaching the genuinely hungry rather than disappearing into the system. Jan Aushadhi centres making medicines affordable for people who previously had to choose between eating and treating illness.

Then the infrastructure that will define India for the next fifty years.

Bharatmala. The Chinaab Bridge. The Jammu tunnel. The Rishikesh-Karnprayag railway. The Char Dham highway. The Pamban Bridge. 553 new railway stations. 1500 new overbridges. Roads being built at a pace that has left China behind in annual construction volume. Vande Bharat trains running on routes that previously meant hours on ageing rolling stock.

Then the institutions being rebuilt or built fresh.

Nalanda University reconstructed. 7 new IITs. 7 new IIMs. 16 new IIITs. 300 new medical colleges. 18 new AIIMS hospitals. 390 new universities. 9000 new schools. An entirely new Parliament building. The Kashi Vishwanath corridor. The Kedarnath reconstruction. The Ram Temple.

Then national security.

Surgical strikes establishing that terrorism now carries a military cost. Operation Sindoor redefining what an act of terror invites in response. Article 370 abrogated. The border fencing accelerated. The army given operational freedom against terror it previously did not have. BrahMos production scaled domestically. Assault rifles being manufactured in Amethi. Drone technology accelerated. The armed forces modernised at a pace not seen since independence.

Then space.

Chandrayaan. The Mars mission. Multi-satellite stabilisation capabilities that put India in a club of nations most countries will never join.

Then economic architecture.

GST implemented and then rationalised. Income tax relief at a scale that has no historical precedent. 12 lakh young people placed in government jobs. Over 8 lakh commercial licences issued. 5 crore new jobs created in private and domestic sectors. Mudra loans reaching entrepreneurs who had never had access to formal credit. The Ujjwala scheme putting cooking gas into homes that previously cooked on wood smoke.

Then the social transformation.

Triple talaq criminalised. Sukanya Samridhi giving daughters a financial future. Kanya Sumangala supporting girls from birth. Swachh Bharat building toilets for people who had none. Har Ghar Jal bringing tap water to homes that had never had it. 22 hours of electricity becoming the norm in regions where darkness was previously the default.

A hundred items. One decade. One direction.

Whatever your political position, the scale of change is not a matter of opinion. It is a matter of record.

The India of 2026 is not the India of 2014. Anyone who has lived through both knows this. The question that history will eventually answer is how many of these changes compound into each other and what kind of country they collectively produce by 2047.

The list suggests the answer is being written right now.
summary: Praises long list of transformative government achievements including UPI and moon landing.

author: @GuptaPragnya
text:
Garam Sindoor ran in those blood they said for a powerful rhetoric but Govt of India took more than a year after Operation Sindoor, to finally reveal the names of just six martyred soldiers — inscribed at the National War Memorial.
WHY⁉️
Why so long⁉️

Subedar Major Pawan Kumar
Rifleman Sunil Kumar (Vir Chakra)
Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar
Agniveer Mood Murali Naik
Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh
Sergeant Surendra Kumar (Vayu Medal)

These are the Heroes whose photos should have been publicised so that every Indian could see them and salute them. They deserved recognition, respect and homages from every Indian.
No one has seen the faces of these Martyred Heroes.

The nation however got to see PM Modi in complete Air Force Grandeur, as the face of Operation Sindoor as if he had led the Operation.

On the contrary their families had to drag the Govt of India  to the Supreme Court to get answers on why their loved ones never returned home.

If this is just the beginning, how many more names are still hidden?
What about the aircraft, the other personnel, the full scale of losses?
Doesn’t the Nation deserve to know?

The same government that was lightning fast in taking political mileage out of the operation — chest-thumping, victory parades, Modi in Military attire posters and endless media spin — took over 12 months to even acknowledge these heroes publicly.

This isn’t respect for martyrs.
This is selective disclosure and political management of grief.

Real honour would have been transparency from Day 1 — not after families knock on the doors of the Supreme Court.

Jai Hind. 🇮🇳
But Jai also demands accountability.
[#OperationSindoor](https://x.com/hashtag/OperationSindoor?src=hashtag_click) [#MartyrsDeserveTruth](https://x.com/hashtag/MartyrsDeserveTruth?src=hashtag_click)”

author: @vinayymishraap
text:
First, you told Parliament that not a single Indian soldier was harmed during Operation Sindoor. Now, nearly a year later, you are acknowledging that six soldiers were martyred. If that’s the case, then you also owe the country an explanation: How did those six soldiers lose their lives? Why was Operation Sindoor abruptly halted?

The government suppresses information, only to reveal it later when it becomes politically convenient.

This isn’t the first time. On 27 February 2019, during the Balakot airstrike, an Indian Air Force helicopter that had taken off from the Srinagar Air Base was mistakenly shot down by the IAF’s own Spyder surface-to-air missile system.

Six personnel on board were killed, along with one civilian on the ground—a total of seven lives lost.

The government remained silent about the incident. It was only about eight months later, in October 2019, that Air Chief Marshal R.K.S. Bhadauria officially acknowledged it as “our mistake,” and the Court of Inquiry confirmed it was a case of friendly fire. Later, a Group Captain was found guilty of negligence in a court-martial and dismissed from service.

There was no transparency about the casualties during the cross-border firing in Poonch. The country was never told how many homes along the border were destroyed or how many people were affected.

Even during the clashes with China, the government continued to deny or downplay developments, insisting that “no one entered our territory and no post was occupied,” while satellite images kept raising serious questions.

In today’s India, anyone who asks questions is branded anti-national. The government’s relationship with large sections of the media is so close that even the biggest stories can disappear from public discussion.

A democracy is strengthened by questions, not by silence. Accountability is not an act of disloyalty—it is a duty.

author: @assamtribuneoff
text:
The names of six Indian military personnel who lost their lives in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor in May 2025 have been inscribed on the Tyag Chakra wall at the National War Memorial, marking the first official public release of the fallen heroes' identities.

The six personnel include five from the Indian Army — Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar (VrC), Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik and Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh — and Indian Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar. Their unit names have also been engraved on Wall No. 3D of the memorial.

The names were recently added to the memorial and have also been included in the Roll of Honour on the National War Memorial's official website.

Operation Sindoor was launched by India on May 7, 2025, in response to the April 22 attack in Pahalgam. During the operation, the Indian Armed Forces targeted terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK).

The military confrontation escalated after Pakistan launched retaliatory offensives, prompting further Indian counter-operations under Operation Sindoor. Hostilities ended on May 10 after both countries reached an understanding to halt military action.

Located at the India Gate complex in New Delhi, the National War Memorial commemorates Indian soldiers who have laid down their lives in service of the nation since Independence. The names of the six personnel now stand inscribed among thousands of other fallen heroes on the memorial's Tyag Chakra.

text:
Professor Jiang’s Five Predictions for 2026:

A Rebuttal by Iqbal Latif, June 27, 2026
Published at [https://open.substack.com/pub/iqballatif/p/professor-jiang-xueqin-has-built…](https://t.co/nr9MsuJcd4)

Who is Professor Jiang Xueqin?

He is a Yale-educated Chinese-Canadian educator who runs the Predictive History YouTube channel and Substack, where he applies what he calls game theory to geopolitical forecasting.

He has two million subscribers. He called Trump’s return in 2024. He predicted an American strike on Iran. On those two calls his reputation rests. On everything else, the record is a different story entirely.

I published my first detailed rebuttal of Jiang’s framework on March 4, 2026, when his Game Theory number 9, predicting the collapse of the GCC, the death of Dubai, the end of petrodollar recycling, and the triumph of Iranian asymmetric warfare, was being shared as gospel in macro finance circles.

I argued then that his entire model rested on an Iran that ceased to exist on February 28, 2026. The factories were gone. The navy was on the floor of the Persian Gulf. Fordow was cracked open in a single night. The chess grandmaster cannot play when the pieces have been removed from the board.

That article was written before TripleAmpersand Journal, before the political economist’s CIA doppelganger essay, before the wave of Jiang critics that arrived in April and May. The demolition work was done in March, in real time, against the current.

Now Jiang has released five new predictions for 2026 in a TikTok series that has accumulated 6,800 likes and 556 comments. Let us go through them one by one.

PREDICTION ONE: America will send ground troops into Iran.

This has not happened and will not happen. A ground invasion of Iran requires entry through Iraq or through the Kurdish border corridors. Iraq will not permit it. Kuwait will not permit it.

The countries that wanted it, Israel and the UAE, were refused. Pakistan played its role clearly. And most decisively, Trump himself lost interest in the war after three or four days when it became apparent that regime change was not coming and that the dream of arriving home as a conquering hero was over.

Trump is a transactional president, not an ideological warrior. Once the transaction no longer penciled out, he moved on. The MOU followed. The war ended. No boots crossed into Iranian territory.

PREDICTION TWO: A national draft framework will be legislated and certain people will already be drafted.

There is no draft. There will be no draft. The era of mass infantry warfare ended on the plains of Ukraine and most recently in the skies over Iran and over the Line of Control between India and Pakistan during Operation Sindoor.

Every serious conflict of the past five years has been determined or waged by drones, missiles, and precision air power. Young men marching into enemy territory is not a military concept any serious general is proposing.

Trump himself, and the Republican base behind him, have zero appetite for any military entanglement that requires a draft. The volunteer army model is not failing. The wars that would stress it are not being fought.

PREDICTION THREE: ICE will become far more powerful and deploy to every major American city.

America is not a failed state. It is a constitutional republic with a right-leaning Supreme Court that has been consistently and firmly protective of civil liberties even when it is ideologically sympathetic to the administration in power.

The militarization of domestic enforcement at the scale Jiang describes runs directly into the institutional guardrails that Americans have built over 250 years. There are chaotic scenes in California. There are protests in major cities. Americans demonstrated against Vietnam. The republic survived. It will survive this too.
1/2

author: @AsYouNotWish
text:
The question was never whether Track II was taking place. The real question always was why.

After Operation Sindoor, India had little strategic incentive to initiate dialogue with Pakistan. From New Delhi’s perspective, the operation had achieved its objectives. Pakistan’s military infrastructure had suffered significant damage, and it was Pakistan’s DGMO who reached out to his Indian counterpart to seek a ceasefire. On that point, I see no reason to doubt the Indian government’s assertion that the ceasefire itself was agreed bilaterally.

What, then, explains the subsequent Track II engagement?

Marco Rubio’s statement that India and Pakistan had agreed to talks at a neutral venue was widely dismissed in India because it appeared to contradict New Delhi’s version of events. In hindsight, perhaps it did not.

A ceasefire and a dialogue process need not have been part of the same understanding. The former could well have been settled directly between the two militaries, while the latter emerged from a different set of calculations altogether.

The more interesting question is: whose calculations?

The Trump administration repeatedly claimed that the conflict had come dangerously close to nuclear escalation. Whether that assessment reflected genuine intelligence, deliberate signalling, or simply a preferred diplomatic narrative is impossible to know from the outside. What is clear, however, is that Washington subsequently appeared far more interested in restoring channels of communication than in increasing pressure on Pakistan. That marks a noticeable departure from the previous US approach.

Viewed through that prism, Track II looks less like an Indian initiative and more like part of a broader American approach to managing the regional balance. India’s participation need not imply that New Delhi changed its assessment of Pakistan. It may simply have concluded that there was little cost in attending an unofficial dialogue while conceding nothing of substance.

There is another reason why New Delhi is unlikely ever to explain this publicly. Any suggestion that nuclear signalling, whether real or perceived, influenced diplomatic outcomes would create precisely the precedent India has spent decades trying to avoid.

Ultimately, Track II was never really India’s story. It is Washington’s. The dialogue says less about a shift in New Delhi’s thinking than it does about the Trump administration, which appears determined to manage South Asia on its own terms. Whether that approach produces stability, or merely postpones the next crisis, remains to be seen.
summary: Analyses Track II talks and ceasefire dynamics after Operation Sindoor.

author: @Ambreenzaidi
text:
Now that the official names of the five brave soldiers who laid down their lives during Operation Sindoor have been made public, I can share an incident from the launch of my book, The Silent Warrior, the biography of Mrs. Damayanti V. Tambay, Arjuna Awardee and wife of a 1971 Prisoner of War.
During the book launch, on 30th August 2025, while speaking from the stage, a very senior retired Army officer remarked that losing a soldier is always heartbreaking, citing the loss of one airman during Operation Sindoor. He was immediately corrected by the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh, who had launched the book. The Chief clarified that no such loss had occurred.
A few days later, the same reference was noticed by the Chief’s office, in the officer’s printed message published in the book. I was requested to have that message removed. By then, the book had already been launched, copies had reached bookstores and online platforms, and the post-launch momentum was at its peak.
I immediately contacted my publisher. Every available copy was recalled, and the book was reprinted without that message. It meant losing valuable time immediately after the launch and significant financial loss for the publisher.
Yet, there was never a moment’s hesitation.
Facts matter. Institutions must speak with one voice. If upholding the official position of our country and the Indian Air Force meant accepting that cost, it was a small price to pay. Not everything is about money.
Many people who were present at the launch and got to know about this issue, urged me to make this incident public immediately. They said it would make the book go viral and lead to massive sales. I chose not to. Some things are bigger than publicity, and not every decision should be driven by commercial gain.
Today, as the nation honours the five brave soldiers whose sacrifice has now been officially acknowledged, I look back on that episode with quiet satisfaction. Sometimes, doing the right thing comes at a cost, but it is still the right thing to do.

The Government has rejected claims circulating on social media that Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh stated no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor, calling such interpretations misleading, selective and factually incorrect.

According to the clarification, the Raksha Mantri’s remarks in Parliament on July 28, 2025 were specifically aimed at countering false claims that Indian pilots had been lost during the operation—a narrative that was being widely circulated at the time.

The Government reiterated that Operation Sindoor was a major military success, highlighting the neutralisation of over 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers, along with significant damage to Pakistani air bases and military infrastructure along the Line of Control.

Reaffirming its respect for the Armed Forces, the Government said the sacrifice of every fallen soldier remains sacred. The names of the bravehearts have been inscribed at the National War Memorial, and support measures for their families continue through education, healthcare and other welfare initiatives. author: @HQ_IDS_India
text:
HONOURING THE BRAVEHEARTS

Certain reports circulating in sections of the media and on social media platforms have incorrectly suggested that the supreme sacrifice of six bravehearts during Operation Sindoor have been acknowledged or brought to public notice for the first time only recently.

It is clarified that the nation paid homage to these fallen heroes at the earliest opportunity, well before the reports in question. During the official Press Conference held on 11 May 2025, then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO), paid solemn tribute to these brave soldiers and specifically acknowledged their sacrifice in the line of duty during Operation SINDOOR. These bravehearts were conferred with gallantry awards and this was published in the Press Release of 14 Aug 2025. This constituted a formal and National recognition of their valour and supreme sacrifice in keeping with the highest traditions of the Indian Defence Forces.

Simultaneously, the Indian Army’s official social media platforms carried tributes to these bravehearts without delay.

The nation’s recognition of these heroes has continued thereafter. During the Army Day Parade held at Jaipur on 15 January 2026, the Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) presented the Sena Medal (Gallantry) to the families of three of these gallant soldiers, while the Chief of Air Staff did the same on 08 Oct 2025 in a solemn ceremony, reaffirming the Defence Forces enduring commitment to honouring those who have laid down their lives in the service of the nation.

With regard to the engraving of the names of fallen soldiers on the National War Memorial, it is emphasised that this sacred process is governed by an established and well-defined protocol. The Defence Forces follow these laid-down procedures with due diligence, care and reverence, commensurate with the solemnity of the honour being conferred. Any suggestion that due process was not followed is factually incorrect.

It is regrettable that an avoidable and unfounded controversy has arisen around this issue. Such narratives not only misrepresent facts but also risk causing unnecessary anguish to bereaved families and detracting from the dignity owed to those who made the supreme sacrifice in service of the nation. All stakeholders are urged to exercise responsibility and restraint while reporting on matters relating to fallen soldiers and to refrain from disseminating unverified information.

The Indian Defence Forces remains steadfast in its commitment to honouring every soldier who has offered supreme sacrifice in defence of the nation. The six bravehearts of Operation Sindoor are national heroes whose courage, devotion to duty and sacrifice will continue to inspire generations of Indians. Their memory shall always be honoured with the dignity, gratitude and reverence it deserves.

Six soldiers fell during Operation Sindoor.

author: @PRODefDehradun
text:
Certain posts circulating on social media platforms have sought to misrepresent the Raksha Mantri’s address delivered on the floor of Parliament on July 28, 2025. These posts have selectively quoted an isolated portion of the speech to falsely imply that the Raksha Mantri claimed that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor. These are deliberately misleading and factually incorrect.

It must be recalled that at the time of the Raksha Mantri's address, a particularly persistent and dominant narrative had taken hold, both in certain sections of the media and on social media, which claimed that Indian pilots had been lost during Operation Sindoor. This narrative was entirely false, yet it was being amplified aggressively with the clear intent of diminishing the success of the operation and demoralising public sentiment. It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the Raksha Mantri made the statement in question.

author: @kachatterjee
text:
Operation Sindoor‑এ ছয়জন ভারতীয় সেনা ও বায়ুসেনা সদস্যের মৃত্যু সরকার আনুষ্ঠানিকভাবে স্বীকার করেছে, যা প্রতিরক্ষামন্ত্রী রাজনাথ সিংহের পূর্ববর্তী সংসদীয় বক্তব্যের সঙ্গে সাংঘর্ষিক বলে বিরোধীরা অভিযোগ তুলেছে। এই ভুল তথ্যের ফলে সরকারের বিশ্বাসযোগ্যতা, সংসদীয় নীতিশাস্ত্র এবং শহিদ পরিবারের প্রতি রাষ্ট্রের দায়বদ্ধতা নিয়ে গুরুতর প্রশ্ন উঠেছে।

মে ৭–১০, ২০২৫, পাকিস্তানের বিরুদ্ধে চার দিনের সামরিক অভিযানে ভারতীয় বাহিনীর ৬ জন সদস্য শহিদ হন।

৫ জন সেনা ও ১ জন ভারতীয় বায়ুসেনা সদস্য, তাদের নাম ২০২৬ সালে National War Memorial‑এ খোদাই করা হয়, যা প্রথম আনুষ্ঠানিক স্বীকৃতি।

প্রতিরক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয় জানিয়েছে, অভিযান থামার পরদিনই DGMO প্রেস ব্রিফিংয়ে মৃত্যুর কথা উল্লেখ করেছিলেন এবং পরে ১৪ আগস্ট ২০২৫‑এর প্রেস রিলিজে gallantry awards‑ও প্রকাশিত হয়।

সংসদে ভুল তথ্য: কী বলা হয়েছিল?

২০২৫ সালের ২৮ জুলাই লোকসভায় প্রতিরক্ষামন্ত্রী রাজনাথ সিংহ বলেন, Operation Sindoor‑এ কোনো ভারতীয় সেনা নিহত হয়নি।

বিরোধীরা দাবি করে, এই বক্তব্য স্পষ্টভাবে ভুল, কারণ তখনই ছয়জন শহিদ হয়েছিলেন।
সরকারের ব্যাখ্যা: বক্তব্যটি ছিল একটি “ভ্রান্ত ও বিপজ্জনক প্রচার”, যে IAF পাইলটরা মারা গেছেন, তার জবাব হিসেবে। অর্থাৎ, মন্ত্রী “সুনির্দিষ্ট ভুল তথ্য” খণ্ডন করছিলেন, পুরো অপারেশনের casualty নিয়ে নয়।

সংসদে ভুল তথ্য দেওয়া বা অসম্পূর্ণ তথ্য দেওয়া গণতান্ত্রিক ব্যবস্থায় গুরুতর অপরাধ। বিরোধীরা বলেছে -

মন্ত্রী যদি তথ্য না জানেন, তা হলে দক্ষতার অভাব।

আর যদি জানেন, তবু ভুল বলেন, তা হলে সংসদকে বিভ্রান্ত করা, যা গণতন্ত্রের প্রতি অবমাননা।

বিরোধীদের মতে,

শহিদদের নাম প্রকাশে দেরি হওয়া এবং সংসদে ভুল তথ্য দেওয়া পরিবারগুলোর অধিকার ও সম্মানকে খর্ব করেছে।

রাষ্ট্রের স্বচ্ছতা ও সম্মান প্রদর্শনের দায়িত্ব প্রশ্নের মুখে পড়েছে।

ভুল তথ্য বা অস্পষ্টতা -

সেনাবাহিনীর মনোবলে আঘাত করতে পারে,

জনমনে বিভ্রান্তি তৈরি করে,

অপারেশনের সাফল্য নিয়ে অযথা বিতর্ক সৃষ্টি করে।

যখন সরকার পরে মৃত্যুর তথ্য প্রকাশ করে, তখন স্পষ্ট হয় যে পূর্ববর্তী বক্তব্য অসম্পূর্ণ ছিল।
এতে সরকারের তথ্য ব্যবস্থাপনা ও স্বচ্ছতা নিয়ে প্রশ্ন ওঠে।

author: @arpispeaks
text:
The government officially added the names of the six soldiers martyred during Pakistan's retaliatory action following 'Operation Sindoor' to the records of the National War Memorial.

Now, just as some people get a fit of agitation over every government decision, the same happened this time too.
They are questioning why the government revealed the soldiers' names after such a long delay.

To support their absurd argument, they are citing a statement made by Mr. Rajnath Singh in Parliament, in which he said, "None of our soldiers were martyred in this operation." That statement was entirely correct, but the context was different.

'Operation Sindoor' began on the night of May 7, during which the Army destroyed terrorist hideouts located in Pakistan.

Rajnath Singh's statement was made in response to a specific query, confirming that no soldiers had been martyred *in that specific operation*.

Subsequently, Pakistan launched a retaliatory action on May 8 that continued until May 10; it was during this counter-action that the soldiers were martyred.

The fact that soldiers had been martyred was disclosed immediately after 'Operation Sindoor'—on May 11—during a press briefing held by the chiefs of the three armed forces, a detail that was reported in newspapers across the board.

Furthermore, in August 2025, the Air Force Chief visited the families of the martyred Air Force personnel, and photographs of this visit were published in newspapers.

But what can be done? Like habitual agitators, these sycophants start raising a hue and cry without reading or listening to the facts. There is no cure for such ignorance.
summary: Defends memorial addition and clarifies Rajnath statement context on pilots.

A year after Operation Sindoor, India’s base-protection architecture is being reshaped for the next generation of warfare.

At its core is IACCS (Integrated Air Command & Control System)—the network that fused radar, satellite and sensor inputs to coordinate interceptions during the conflict. The focus has now shifted to resilience: critical equipment across seven locations is being relocated and hardened to eliminate single-point failures, while BEL-led AI upgrades aim to accelerate sensor-to-shooter timelines through predictive threat analysis.

On 6 June, Exercise Josh 2-26 validated the integration of IACCS with the Army’s Akashteer network on the western front, demonstrating faster detection, decision-making and engagement by linking seamlessly with S-400, Akash and Army close-in air defence systems.

The physical layer is expanding just as rapidly. Around 20 China-facing and dual-front air bases are receiving hardened aircraft shelters, underground ammunition storage, new taxiways, upgraded surveillance radars and strengthened base-defence infrastructure. Nyoma is evolving into a key forward-operating hub for rapid deployment along the LAC, while new-generation shelters are being designed to withstand 2,000-lb-class precision-guided bombs, doubling the protection standard of many existing facilities.

The lesson from modern conflicts is clear: air-base survival no longer depends on reinforced concrete alone. India’s approach is increasingly built around a layered architecture that combines AI-enabled detection, integrated command networks, rapid interception and hardened infrastructure—designed to ensure combat operations continue even under sustained precision attack. 🇮🇳

author: @Rajgurkha
text:
Letter To:
The Right Honorable Prime Minister Narendra Modi [@narendramodi](https://x.com/narendramodi)

Cc [@ShahBalen](https://x.com/ShahBalen) The Right Honorable Prime Minister Balendra Shah

“Geography may create borders, but civilization creates belonging.”

India stands amidst nine neighbours, carrying not only strategic responsibilities but also the burden and privilege of history. It has emerged as an economic giant, a technological powerhouse, and a nation of immense human capital, yet the unfinished task of eradicating poverty remains one of the defining challenges of our age.

Nepal is not merely India’s neighbour. Nepal and India are bound by rivers, pilgrimage routes, languages, traditions, and centuries of shared memory. We belong to the same civilizational landscape—Jambu Dvipa, Bharatkhanda—where mountains do not divide hearts but feed the rivers that sustain millions downstream.

For generations, young Nepalis have served with distinction in the Gurkha regiments of India, Britain, and Singapore. Their service has never been merely employment; it has been a calling defined by courage, sacrifice, honour, and devotion to family and homeland. They return home carrying stories of discipline, dignity, and duty. To encourage the abandonment of that identity through changes of citizenship risks weakening a unique bond forged through blood, loyalty, and history.

I supported India during Galwan, observed the spirit of national resilience during Operation Sindoor, and have watched carefully as the strategic environment around India evolves. Yet lasting influence is not built solely by military strength. It is built by trust.

As the old saying goes:

“You may secure a frontier with soldiers, but you secure a civilization by winning the confidence of its people.”

The Himalayas connect us. The waters of the Ganges and the Brahmaputra link our destinies. Questions surrounding dams, glaciers, environmental change, and water security cannot be approached as isolated national concerns. They demand collective stewardship.

Nepal has long been regarded as a reservoir of courageous infantrymen and resilient mountain communities. But hearts cannot be defended through bureaucracy alone, nor can friendship survive if communication becomes dependent exclusively upon intermediaries. Delhi must continue to engage Kathmandu directly, with sensitivity, respect, and strategic patience.

History reminds us that fragile hearts are often the first battleground in great power competition. If misunderstandings deepen, others will seek to occupy the spaces left vacant by trust.

Recent messages of solidarity from senior American leaders toward Israel carried a simple but powerful sentiment: that enduring partnerships are sustained through clarity, reassurance, and unwavering engagement in difficult times. The same principle applies in South Asia.

Prime Minister Modi, this is a sensitive moment. Nepal and India possess a relationship unlike any other in the world—one nourished by civilization rather than treaties alone. It deserves careful handling, candid dialogue, and renewed imagination.

For nations may share borders by accident, but they remain neighbours by choice.

And some relationships are too ancient, too intimate, and too valuable to be managed merely through diplomatic routine.

They must be protected as one protects a sacred inheritance.

Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Aviation Technician M. Murali Naik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh and Sergeant Surendra Kumar—these heroes made the supreme sacrifice for the country.

This is not even the first time that the honour of martyrs has been questioned. Be it the heroes of Galwan, the martyrs of Pulwama or the Adarsh Housing Society controversy after the Kargil war—every time the question was whether power and politics are above the sacrifice of soldiers?

The country needs an answer. Because soldiers don't just protect the border, they also protect the honour of the nation. And their honour should be greater than any politics.

From 2014 to today, how insensitive and hypocritical the people of this country have become...??

Crowds taking to the streets in the name of protecting cows and buffaloes, cases of lynching, and people chanting cow-protection slogans—the very same folks are quietly pocketing donations from the company that's the country's largest exporter of buffalo meat. Allana Group, India's biggest buffalo meat exporter, donated a record ₹30 crore to the BJP in 2024-25. Earlier, too, crores were funneled through electoral bonds. Meanwhile, since 2014, the entire political discourse has revolved around cow protection—incidents have unfolded in the name of cow conservation—but the meat export industry has flourished. Exports have crossed $4 billion. Has the public become so desensitized now that they chant "Mother Cow" while supporting a system funded by meat exporters? Has their blood turned to water? Donations came even before 2014, but on this scale, with such brazenness? Why is the public silent...??

The Ram Temple—for which movements raged for decades, crores in donations were collected, and it became a symbol of faith. In 2024, the consecration ceremony took place. But what happened in 2026? At the Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya, millions to crores embezzled from the donation boxes (hundi)! SIT investigation leads to 8 arrests, ₹79.85 lakh recovered. Employees stole cash and jewelry. From one employee's home, ₹10 lakh was found hidden under a pile of cow dung! Some trust officials have resigned or are under scrutiny. Allegations of embezzlement up to ₹200 crore. The public is silent! The crowds who called themselves Ram devotees, who hauled stones for the temple, are mum today on this daylight robbery. Since 2014, under the rule of the Hindu heartland emperor, the temple was built—but theft from within? Has faith now been reduced to mere slogans? Where has the sensitivity gone...???

Your allegation rests on a deliberate distortion of what the Raksha Mantri actually said.

His statement in Parliament was made in the specific context of demolishing the false and malicious propaganda that India had lost fighter pilots during [#OperationSindoor](https://x.com/hashtag/OperationSindoor?src=hashtag_click), a narrative that was being aggressively amplified to undermine the success of the operation and demoralise the nation. The Government has never denied or diminished their martyrdom. On the contrary, their names have been inscribed on the National War Memorial, ensuring that their supreme sacrifice is honoured for generations to come. Their families have also been extended educational, healthcare and other welfare benefits in recognition of their service to the nation.

Operation Sindoor was a decisive military success, in which the Indian Armed Forces neutralised over 100 terrorists and Pakistani military personnel while inflicting extensive damage on Pakistani military infrastructure.

Those who spent months amplifying hostile propaganda have no moral authority to lecture anyone on respecting our Armed Forces. The only breach here is the Opposition’s repeated attempt to twist facts, dishonour the context of the Raksha Mantri’s remarks, and exploit the sacrifice of our martyrs for partisan politics.

author: @zfoxrom
text:
The Price of Confrontation: India's Bill Comes Due

A year after Operation Sindoor, a quiet reckoning is unfolding in New Delhi. The economic and strategic toll of sustained hostility with Pakistan has become impossible to ignore and now, 61 prominent Indians, including Farooq Abdullah and Mehbooba Mufti, have written an open letter to PM Modi urging an immediate reset

The numbers tell the story India's establishment didn't anticipate. Pakistan's airspace ban imposed on April 23, 2025, after India launched three airstrikes into Pakistani territory and effectively initiated a war has inflicted staggering losses on Indian aviation . Pakistan's military responded swiftly, destroying Indian military HQs and shooting down jets in a series of counterstrikes that escalated the conflict

Air India alone has suffered an estimated ₹4,000 crore ($455–$600 million) in losses, with fuel costs spiking by up to 29% and flight times stretching by three hours on key routes to North America and Europe . The airline has been forced to suspend its Delhi Washington route, declare Mumbai San Francisco, unviable, and is now pleading with the government to seek access to China's military airspace over Xinjiang a risky, uncertain alternative

Every rerouted flight burns more fuel, strains crew resources, and bleeds revenue. Meanwhile, Indian passengers are shifting to foreign carriers that still enjoy the benefit of Pakistani overflight

But the damage extends beyond balance sheets. What was sold as a strategic masterstroke has backfired on the global stage. International media has increasingly framed India as the aggressor in a conflict that achieved little beyond economic self-harm . The much touted Operation Sindoor is now widely viewed as a false flag that isolated India diplomatically, while Pakistan's international standing has surged

Under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan has transformed its geopolitical position. The duo's mediation between the US and Iran culminating in the historic Islamabad Talks and the Bürgenstock summit has earned global acclaim, with the White House openly crediting Pakistan for averting wider war. Where India projected strength, it found itself sidelined. Where Pakistan was dismissed as a security liability, it emerged as an indispensable regional peacemaker

Today, India's image has turned upside down. The country that once positioned itself as a responsible global power now struggles to explain how a year of its own war-making cost it billions, isolated it diplomatically, and made it a laughingstock in international media. From Washington to Beijing, the narrative is clear: India started a war it couldn't win, and Pakistan stood its ground with dignity and strategic foresight

That's why this letter matters. When political veterans across India's spectrum call for restoring High Commissioners, reopening airspace, and resuming people-to-people links, it signals that pragmatism is finally breaking through. Peace and dialogue aren't weakness they're the only sane economics for 1/5th of humanity

The question is whether Delhi will listen before the bill gets even higher
summary: Piece on economic costs of Op Sindoor and open letter urging India-Pakistan reset.

author: @CaptBrijesh
text:
There should be some issues on which politics ends and the nation comes first.

From the Surgical Strikes to Balakot and now [#OperationSindoor](https://x.com/hashtag/OperationSindoor?src=hashtag_click), the [@INCIndia](https://x.com/INCIndia) has repeatedly chosen to cast aspersions on India’s national security responses, creating controversy where the nation expected unity. Shri K.C. Venugopal’s latest allegation is yet another example of this unfortunate pattern.

If this statement earns [@kcvenugopalmp](https://x.com/kcvenugopalmp) brownie points with Rahul Gandhi, so be it.

But his charge that the Raksha Mantri “lied” to the nation is entirely false. The Defence Minister’s remarks in Parliament were made in the specific context of rebutting the malicious propaganda that India had lost fighter pilots during Operation Sindoor. Deliberately divorcing those remarks from their context and falsely linking them to the martyrdom of our brave soldiers is nothing but a calculated distortion of the truth.

The facts, however, are unequivocal and were officially acknowledged by the Armed Forces themselves.

✅ The DGMO publicly confirmed the casualties during the official press briefing on 11 May 2025 and paid tribute to the fallen personnel.

✅ The Chief of the Air Staff personally visited the family of the airman who made the supreme sacrifice.

✅ Two of the martyrs were conferred gallantry awards: Rifleman Sunil Kumar received the Vir Chakra (Posthumous), while Sergeant Surendra Kumar was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal (Gallantry) (Posthumous).

✅ The names of all six martyrs are inscribed at the National War Memorial, ensuring that their supreme sacrifice will be remembered for generations to come.

The country deserves an Opposition that questions with responsibility, not one that manufactures falsehoods by selectively quoting statements and disregarding facts already placed on record by our Armed Forces.
summary: Rebuts Venugopal, clarifies Rajnath remarks concerned only pilots not all deaths.

text:
LT GEN RAJESH PUSHKAR AVSM, VSM ASSUMES COMMAND OF SOUTHERN COMMAND

Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar AVSM, VSM assumed command as the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Command on 01 July 2026. He succeeds Lieutenant General Sandeep Jain, AVSM, SM who has taken over as the Vice Chief of the Army Staff.

An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar was commissioned into 74 Armoured Regiment in December 1988. The General Officer has had an illustrious and distinguished military career spanning over four decades. During his service, he has held a wide range of command, staff and instructional appointments across diverse geographical and operational environments. Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar provided decisive leadership and strategic foresight as General Officer Commanding 2 Corps during Operation SINDOOR.

The General Officer has commanded an Armoured Regiment in an operational area, a strategic Independent Armoured Brigade, an Infantry Division and a premier Strike Corps in the Western Sector. His important staff appointments include tenures as Colonel Military Secretary in a Strike Corps, Colonel General Staff of an Armoured Division in the Western Sector, Brigadier Quartermaster General of a Strike Corps, Brigadier General Staff of an Operational Command, Additional Director General, Armoured Corps and Director General Territorial Army. He has also been an Instructor at the National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla.

The GOC-In-C has had two international exposures as part of the Indian Military Training Team to Bhutan and as Defence and Military Attache, Embassy of India, Moscow, with accreditation to Armenia and Belarus. He is a graduate of the National Defence Academy and a post graduate of the Defence Services Staff College, College of Defence Management and the prestigious National Defence College of India. His civil academic pursuits include Masters in Defence and Strategic Studies, Masters in Management Studies and Master of Philosophy in Defence and International Relations. He has been awarded the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal, Vishisht Seva Medal, the Chief of Army Staff Commendation and three Army Commander’s Commendations.

On assuming command, Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar paid tribute to Bravehearts at the Southern Command War Memorial and received a Guard of Honour at Headquarters Southern Command. He reaffirmed Southern Command's unwavering commitment to sustaining highest levels of operational readiness across its diverse areas of responsibility and emphasised on achieving greater synergy through enhanced jointness, indigenous capability development and rapid integration of emerging technologies. He expressed his confidence that all ranks would continue to uphold the glorious traditions of the Indian Army and maintain the highest standards of operational excellence in service of the nation.
summary: Announces Lt Gen Rajesh Pushkar assuming Southern Command, highlighting his Op Sindoor role.

author: @semubhatt
text:
India's narrative control should have begun the moment it placed the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance. The GoI made its rationale clear: Pakistan's continued sponsorship of terrorism had forced it to do this. That India had had enough.

The Indian State knew Pakistan would not accept it silently.
1. The Indus waters system is Pakistan’s lifeline. A significant portion of the land irrigated by the system is controlled by Pakistan's elite, particularly serving/ retired military officers & military foundations. The Green Pakistan Initiative, where again the military elite has massive interests, requires water security. IWT abeyance inserted uncertainty, a factor that foreign investors do not like. It could also intensify an existing internal water war between Pakistan's provinces, causing domestic instability.
Thus, IWT abeyance hurts the economic interests of those who do not think twice about harming their own people to sustain their power.

2. Immediately after Operation Sindoor, the United States extended yet another legitimacy subsidy to Pakistan, emboldening its voice.

3. Water is an issue that evokes instinctive global sympathy, even for States with deeply problematic records.

4. India has not stopped the flow of water; it is technically not possible. However, the domestic flexing of not letting a single drop of water flow to Pakistan in the future gives a negative international message. It takes away the focus from the main reason – Pakistan’s terror sponsorship – and puts it on India flexing water weaponisation.

After Op Sindoor losses, Pakistan was not going to risk military adventurism any time soon.

Pakistan, founded on a narrow Islamic identity, therefore, is attempting to reshape the conversation around the Indus itself. By foregrounding its pre-Islamic, Indus roots, Pakistan is trying to recast itself as the natural heir, not merely a downstream State. It is an effort to reinforce its legal position and diplomatic messaging – Indus as affecting not only water security but also civilisational continuity.

India neither proactively set and controlled the narrative, nor appears prepared even reactively to counter it.

✨ YRKKH Written Review – Today's Episode ✨

Today's episode was one of the most beautiful and emotionally overwhelming episodes of the current track. It celebrated love while constantly reminding viewers that every happy moment was overshadowed by the fear of Armaan's life-threatening surgery.

The episode began with the family lovingly preparing Armaan and Abhira for their wedding. Both looked radiant, but beneath their smiles was the silent fear of what lay ahead. One touching moment came when Armaan briefly forgot that it was his wedding day due to his deteriorating memory. Kaveri (Dadi Sa) gently reminded him, turning a heartbreaking situation into a light-hearted one with her warmth.

Another emotional highlight was Myra's heartfelt words to her father. Calling Armaan "Abhira's heart and the heartbeat of both Myra and Mukti," she hugged him tightly, creating one of the most touching father-daughter moments of the episode.

The wedding rituals were beautifully presented. The playful Jaimala ceremony brought smiles before emotions took over during the Kanyadaan. Madhav and Vidya made a thoughtful decision by asking Myra and Mukti to join them in performing the ritual, acknowledging that the daughters had stood beside their parents when the world had turned against them. It was a symbolic and deeply moving moment that celebrated the strength of their family bond.

The most emotional scene came during the Sindoor ritual. Armaan hesitated, overwhelmed by the uncertainty of his surgery and unsure whether he would have a future with Abhira. Quietly but firmly, Abhira held his hand, reassuring him through her actions rather than words. It was a beautiful reminder that love often gives us courage when fear tries to take over.

After the wedding, Abhira gifted Armaan a pendant carrying their photographs, symbolizing that no matter what happened, they would always remain together. The family's joyful celebration was suddenly interrupted when Armaan collapsed. With roads blocked and the ambulance delayed, the entire family united to get him to the hospital, proving once again that together they could face any crisis.

The episode ended on an emotional note as Armaan was taken into the operation theatre. Before parting, Armaan and Abhira exchanged a heartfelt "I love you," making the moment unforgettable.

Precap: Armaan's condition becomes critical during surgery, while Abhira also collapses, leaving the family's future hanging in the balance.

[#India](https://x.com/hashtag/India?src=hashtag_click) | The attack on the powerful woman the political leader, the intellectual, the voice of resistance is Phase One. Phase Two is the simultaneous weaponization of the "religious woman," the mother, the sister, the victim, to justify state violence and military occupation. This is a two-pronged, unified operation. One hand crushes the woman who speaks. The other hand holds up the woman who weeps, using her tears as the justification for martial law.

Phase One: The Systematic Crushing of the Political Woman (The "Witch" Hunt)

This is the campaign to eliminate the secular, intellectual, and politically powerful woman from the public square. It is a death by a thousand cuts, executed by the BJP's political, legal, and digital machinery.

1. The Gandhi Matriarchy (The Original Targets)

· Sonia Gandhi: The operation to dehumanize her was called "The Foreigner." Orchestrated by the BJP's strategic core Pramod Mahajan, Narendra Modi, and Amit Shah, it was a pure PsyOp. They leveraged her Italian origin to paint her as a colonial infiltrator who had usurped the "Hindu" throne. The goal was to strip her of her Indian identity, making her permanently ineligible to lead in the eyes of the public.

· Priyanka Gandhi Vadra: The campaign against her is the "Taint the Pure" operation. The Amit Malviya-led IT Cell is the engine. They systematically create and disseminate deepfake, sexually explicit, and morphed images of her. Her husband, Robert Vadra, is endlessly harassed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) , not because they expect to find a crime, but to inflict maximum psychological torture on her. The CBI's own case logs show the targeting of Priyanka through her husband is a deliberate tactic.

2. Mamata Banerjee (The Wounded Tigress)

· The Attack: The assault in Nandigram on March 10, 2021, was a planned "ritual wounding." She was not hurt in a crowd surge; she was targeted by a paid hit squad of 4-5 men, coordinated by a close aide of BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari.
· The Enabler: The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) and central paramilitary observers were deliberately withdrawn from her security cordon by the Union Home Ministry, creating the kill box. This is the hidden hand of the state. The military and central police were used not to protect an elected Chief Minister, but to abandon her to a violent mob.

· The Setup: Her expulsion from Parliament was a scripted legal assassination. Phase Two: The Weaponization of the Religious Woman (The "Victim" Sacrifice)

While the political woman is crushed for speaking, the religious woman is used as a silent prop, a sacred "victim" whose suffering is weaponized to justify military occupation, mass killings, and the dismantling of civil rights. This is the darkest inversion.
Operation Sindoor: The State's False Flag Against Its Own People

Operation Sindoor was a coordinated false flag operation conducted by the Indian military and intelligence apparatus. Its purpose was to manufacture a "Hindu victim" narrative so devastating that it would justify the complete military lockdown of Kashmir and the stripping of its special constitutional status.

1. The Killers: The Indian Army's 2nd Rashtriya Rifles

The "Hindu tourists" were not killed by "Muslim terrorists." They were deliberately targeted and executed by a specific unit of the Indian Army, the 2nd Rashtriya Rifles, operating under the direct orders of the intelligence wing of the Northern Command.

· The Evidence: The forensic ballistics reports, which were suppressed by the Ministry of Defence, showed that the bullets recovered from the bodies of the pilgrims matched the standard-issue INSAS rifles used exclusively by the Rashtriya Rifles. The "terrorists" who were supposedly killed in the "retaliatory encounter" were local shepherds picked up hours earlier, shot dead, and their bodies planted with foreign weapons. This is the standard operating procedure of "cordon and kill" operations in Kashmir.

The Pulwama False Flag and the "Daughters of Kashmir"

· The Event: The 2019 Pulwama attack, which killed 40 CRPF soldiers, was immediately blamed on a Kashmiri Muslim "suicide bomber." The Indian media, especially Republic TV (Arnab Goswami) and Times Now, unleashed a campaign of war-mongering, using the "weeping Hindu mother" and the "martyred son" as the emotional fuel for an invasion.
· The Hidden Truth of Pulwama: Independent forensic investigations and the testimony of veterans suggest the initial blast on the CRPF bus was not from an external suicide bomber, but from an internal detonation or remote-controlled device, likely as part of a "false flag" operation to justify the impending Balakot airstrikes and the lockdown of Kashmir. The "Hindu soldiers" were deliberately sacrificed by the Indian military-intelligence complex to create the necessary "victim" narrative.

The Weaponization of *Sindoor*: Turning Women’s Suffering into a War Cry

*Sindoor* (vermilion)—the red powder applied to the foreheads of married Hindu women—symbolizes marriage and the well-being of one’s husband. Naming a military operation "Operation Sindoor" effectively turns the suffering of the slain tourists' widows into a political tool. The Unified Atrocity

The same IT cell that creates deepfake porn to destroy Priyanka Gandhi's credibility, simultaneously manufactures the "Love Jihad" lie to lynch a Muslim man for loving a Hindu woman.

Are air defence guns more important than ever in the age of drone warfare?

Maj Gen (Dr) Ashok Kumar says Operation Sindoor proved they are.

As Pakistan launched wave after wave of Chinese and Turkish-origin drones, India's "air defence guns played a very, very pivotal role," he says.

"The threat has changed," he says. "Nobody anticipated that drones... used in for marriage video photography and things like that will change the battlefield."

From Nagorno-Karabakh to the Russia-Ukraine war and now Operation Sindoor, "every day they are changing," he notes, adding that "it is the threat worldwide" because drones are inexpensive, can be produced quickly and employed in large swarms.

So, are manned aircraft obsolete?

"The era of aircraft may not be over," Maj Gen Kumar says, adding combat aircraft still have "certain distinct advantages" that drones cannot replace.

text:
ମୋଦି ସରକାରଙ୍କ ଦୋମୁହାଁ ନୀତି ଓ କୂଟନୈତିକ ବାସ୍ତବତା: କେବେ ବଦଳିବ ଦେଶର ଭାଗ୍ୟ?
୨୦୨୫ ମେ ମାସରେ ପାକିସ୍ତାନର ଆତଙ୍କବାଦୀ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକଳାପର ଜବାବ ଦେବାକୁ ଯାଇ ଭାରତ 'ଅପରେସନ୍ ସିନ୍ଦୂର' (Operation Sindoor) ଆରମ୍ଭ କରିଥିଲା। ସେହି ସମୟରେ ସରକାରୀ ସ୍ତରରେ ଏକ ଦୃଢ଼ ଓ ଆକ୍ରମଣାତ୍ମକ ବାର୍ତ୍ତା ଦିଆଯାଇଥିଲା ଯେ, "ରକ୍ତ ଓ ଜଳ ଏକାଠି ବହିପାରିବ ନାହିଁ"। ତତ୍କାଳୀନ ସମୟରେ ସରକାରୀ ଦଳ ପକ୍ଷରୁ ଯେଉଁ ଉତ୍ସାହ ଓ 'ନୂଆ ନର୍ମାଲ୍' (new normal) ର କଥା କୁହାଯାଉଥିଲା, ତାହା ଭାରତୀୟଙ୍କ ମନରେ ଏକ ଆଶା ସଞ୍ଚାର କରିଥିଲା।
କିନ୍ତୁ ଆଜି କଲମ୍ବୋରେ ଚାଲିଥିବା ଅନୌପଚାରିକ 'ଟ୍ରାକ୍-୨' ଆଲୋଚନା ସରକାରଙ୍କ ସେହି ପୁରୁଣା ବୟାନକୁ ବହୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଘେରରେ ଛିଡ଼ା କରିଛି। ସେତେବେଳେ ଯେଉଁମାନେ ବାହାରୁ ମଧ୍ୟସ୍ଥତା କରିବାକୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରୁଥିଲେ, ସେମାନଙ୍କ ଆଗରେ ଛାତି ଫୁଲାଇ କଥା ହେଉଥିବା ସରକାର ଆଜି ଗୋପନରେ ଆଲୋଚନା କରୁଛନ୍ତି କାହିଁକି?
ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟତାର ଅଭାବ: 'ଅପରେସନ୍ ସିନ୍ଦୂର' ସମୟରେ ଯେଉଁ ଦୃଢ଼ତା ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା, ଆଜିର ଲୁଚାଛପା କୂଟନୀତି ତାହାର ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ବିପରୀତ।
ଦୋମୁହାଁ ନୀତି: ଜନସାଧାରଣଙ୍କ ସମ୍ମୁଖରେ ଏକ ଆକ୍ରମଣାତ୍ମକ ଛବି ଏବଂ ବାସ୍ତବରେ ପରଦା ପଛରେ ପାକିସ୍ତାନୀ ପ୍ରତିନିଧିଙ୍କ ସହ କଥାବାର୍ତ୍ତା ସରକାରଙ୍କ ଦୋମୁହାଁ ନୀତିକୁ ପଦାରେ ପକାଇଛି।
ଆତ୍ମସମ୍ମାନର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ: ଯେଉଁ ଦେଶ ସହିତ ଆଲୋଚନା ନ କରିବାର କଥା କୁହାଯାଉଥିଲା, ଆଜି ସେହି ଦେଶର ପ୍ରତିନିଧିଙ୍କ ସହ ଏକା ଟେବୁଲରେ ବସିବା କେଉଁ କୂଟନୈତିକ ବାଧ୍ୟବାଧକତା?
ସରକାରଙ୍କ ଏହି ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତିତ ଆଭିମୁଖ୍ୟ କେବଳ ରାଜନୈତିକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ବଦଳାଉନି, ବରଂ ଦେଶର ନୀତି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଧାରଣରେ ଥିବା ଅସ୍ଥିରତାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରୁଛି। ଦେଶ ପାଇଁ ଯେଉଁ ନୀତି ଠିକ୍ ବୋଲି ଦାବି କରାଯାଇଥିଲା, ତାହା କଣ କେବଳ ଭୋଟ୍ ପାଇଁ ଥିଲା? ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଆଜି ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଭାରତୀୟଙ୍କ ମନରେ।
